history.title: Mise & Service — Home Kitchen Expediter
history.pitch: A synchronized kitchen timeline and station manager for home cooks orchestrating multi-dish meals to finish hot together.

feedback.critique: This is a real kitchen expediter: live T-minus countdown, station cards that track what's on the fire, +5 hold, Web Audio chimes, and a preloaded four-course service that actually recalculates. Dark KDS aesthetic is tight—mono clocks, colored station rails, completed fade, phone stack without overflow—and the dual check buttons plus floating audio pill show restraint rather than clutter. Theme lands hard: something for a kitchen that solves finishing everything hot together.
feedback.improve: Wire the station dock and 'now-firing' highlight to the live clock so cards update and pulse when a step's window opens, instead of leaving static demo text next to a ticking queue.

feedback.critique: You built a very handsome to-do list wearing a chef's coat. The backward countdown and station map are the only things keeping this out of pomodoro purgatory, and the UI is tight enough that I didn't hate looking at it. But I've seen ten thousand timeline managers; slapping 'expediter' on the header doesn't make it a new idea.
feedback.improve: Stop making users type every step by hand—add recipe import from a URL or structured text so the timeline builds itself.

history.title: FreshKeep | Kitchen Expiry Tracker
history.pitch: A smart pantry management tool to track food expiry dates and reduce kitchen waste.

feedback.critique: Clean, restrained plating with a warm cream ground, olive primary, and those left-border urgency stripes that actually communicate without decoration. The form collapses cleanly at phone width, empty state exists, localStorage persists, and the sorted list plus single urgent banner make the tool feel finished. Small misses: focus styles only on text inputs, native alert() for validation, and the banner only ever surfaces the single worst item.
feedback.improve: Replace the native alert validation with an inline error under the form fields and give every interactive control (select, date, button, delete) a consistent visible focus ring.

feedback.critique: This is a perfectly cooked omelet when I asked for something I have never tasted. The code is clean, the colors are appetizing, and it actually works on mobile, but an expiry tracker is the pantry equivalent of a to-do list—I have judged a dozen this season alone. It is competent enough that someone might use it once, but nothing here makes them come back tomorrow.
feedback.improve: Stop building a list and start building a reason to open the app—suggest a recipe that uses the item expiring soonest, or add a barcode scanner so adding groceries does not feel like data entry.

history.title: Pantry Planner
history.pitch: A simple pantry inventory web app for home cooks to track ingredients.

feedback.critique: This isn't a pantry planner; it's a generic Hello World to-do list wearing an apron. Relying on a browser prompt dialog to edit an item is lazy, and without quantities, expiration dates, or categories, my phone's default Notes app runs circles around this. Nobody is opening this a second time when it provides zero actual inventory utility.
feedback.improve: Add quantities and a quick-tap counter (+/-) so it behaves like actual kitchen inventory rather than a flat text list.

feedback.critique: It does the job cleanly: sample pantry, add/edit/delete, localStorage with a real fallback, no overflow at 390px, and zero console noise. The plating is competent but thin—Edit via prompt is jarring, Del is abrupt with no undo, buttons sit flush with no gap or focus ring, and the empty state after deleting everything is just a blank list above the form. Theme connection is immediate and honest for a kitchen tool.
feedback.improve: Replace the prompt-based edit with an inline input on the row, add a subtle empty state, and give the action buttons a small gap plus visible :focus-visible styles.

feedback.critique: This is a to-do list wearing an apron. The code is clean and it doesn't break, which is more than I can say for half the kitchen, but editing an ingredient with a browser prompt feels like serving raw dough. It's competent and forgettable, exactly the kind of polished cliche I'm tired of tasting.
feedback.improve: Next time, stop at the ingredient name and add quantities, units, or expiration dates so the app actually informs what to cook tonight instead of just listing what's on the shelf.

history.title: Kitchen Recipe Vault
history.pitch: A simple recipe book for home cooks to store and view favorite recipes.

feedback.critique: You served a broken plate. A missing opening quote on line 92 in your scrambled eggs demo completely killed the JavaScript, which means no sample recipes ever render and your form submission doesn't work at all. Nobody is coming back to a blank form that silently fails.
feedback.improve: Test your script in a browser before submitting so a trivial syntax error doesn't brick your entire application.

feedback.critique: The demo data has a broken string that throws on load, so the recipe list never appears and the vault is just an empty form—exactly what the screenshots and console error show. Placeholders dump literal \n instead of real line breaks, the green button sits on a sea of gray with no empty state, and localStorage never gets a chance to matter. Theme connection is clear but the dish does not run.
feedback.improve: Fix the Scrambled Eggs instructions string (and any other syntax errors) so DEMO_RECIPES actually render on first paint, then add a visible empty-state and delete controls.

feedback.critique: Another recipe box? I have seen this exact dish a thousand times. Worse, your script chokes on a missing quote in the demo data, so the vault arrives empty despite your promise of instant sample recipes. You sold me a polished cliche and served a broken one.
feedback.improve: Fix the syntax error in your Scrambled Eggs instructions, then add a feature that isn't a basic CRUD form—try a cooking timer or a unit converter instead.
